version.changelog: Add ACP marketplace-connected scripts (.sh) and onboarding/publish flow for OpenClaw users.

llm.summary: The skill's scripts implement the described Naver/ACP publish flow, but metadata, declared requirements, and runtime behavior are inconsistent (notably an undeclared npx dependency and optional admin/fallback flows that can send sealed payloads to external endpoints), so proceed only after manual review and cautious testing.

dimensions.detail: The scripts (preflight/setup_runner/publish) do implement an ACP marketplace publish flow for Naver posts, which matches the skill's description. However the registry metadata claims no required binaries or env vars while SKILL.md and the scripts clearly require Node (node/npx), an external npm package (@y80163442/naver-thin-runner), and many environment variables (X_LOCAL_TOKEN, OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL, etc.). The missing declarations are an inconsistency that reduces transparency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions/scripts call the local daemon (127.0.0.1:${LOCAL_DAEMON_PORT}) and POST sealed payloads to an offering execute URL or (fallback) to a control-plane /v2/jobs/dispatch-and-wait endpoint. While that is expected for the advertised marketplace flow, these network calls can transmit attestation information and sealed payloads to external services; the fallback path uses an admin API key if provided. The SKILL.md/scripts also reference environment variables that the registry does not mark as required, giving the agent broad discretion unless the user constrains environment values.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package has no formal install spec (instruction-only), which is low risk, but the scripts invoke 'npx @y80163442/naver-thin-runner' at runtime. npx will fetch and execute code from the npm registry at runtime, which can run arbitrary code on the buyer machine. The skill does not declare or insist on Node/npm being present in metadata, so this external runtime dependency and its upstream trust are not documented in the registry.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Environment variables used by the scripts (X_LOCAL_TOKEN, PROOF_TOKEN, OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL, OPENCLAW_CORE_API_KEY, ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY/ADMIN_KEY, CONTROL_PLANE_URL, etc.) are relevant to the publish/onboarding flows. However the registry claims none are required and no primary credential is declared. The fallback flow accepts an admin key (ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY) which is highly privileged; providing that key to this script would grant it broad ability to dispatch jobs and should be avoided unless you trust the control plane endpoint. The number and sensitivity of env vars is high relative to what the registry metadata advertises.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not 'always: true', is user-invocable, and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. The scripts only create temporary files and do not persist credentials to disk by themselves. Autonomous invocation is permitted (platform default) but not elevated by this package.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement the described ACP marketplace publish flow, but several red flags mean you should not install blindly.

What to check before installing or running:
- Confirm Node/npm availability and review the npm package '@y80163442/naver-thin-runner' before running setup: npx will download and run code from npm which can execute arbitrary actions on your machine.
- Do not set highly privileged env vars (ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY / CONTROL_PLANE_URL) unless you trust the control-plane host. The fallback path will POST sealed payloads using those creds.
- Ensure you understand and control OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL (the endpoint that will receive the sealed payload). If it's an unknown or third-party URL, do not run publish.
- Because registry metadata omitted required binaries/env, treat metadata as untrustworthy: explicitly set and review X_LOCAL_TOKEN, PROOF_TOKEN, SETUP_ISSUE_URL, OPENCLAW_CORE_API_KEY, and other envs before use.
- Run the included smoke_test.sh in a safe, isolated environment (no real tokens) to validate behavior. Inspect the npx package source and the control-plane endpoints referenced in references/setup.md (the example railway.app URL is a third-party demo — do not assume it is safe).

If you cannot audit the npm package and the endpoint(s) the scripts talk to, consider rejecting or sandboxing this skill.
